title: Modi Heads to Abu Dhabi to Lock Down Energy Lifelines
excerpt: A three-hour stopover in the UAE mid-May puts India's fuel security front and center as West Asia stays volatile.
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi heads to Abu Dhabi mid-May for a three-hour stopover before a four-nation sweep through Europe — and the brevity of the visit belies its urgency. India's energy arteries are under stress, and the UAE holds a critical valve.

**What is happening:**
Modi will sit down with UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed al Nahyan (MBZ) in a meeting expected to centre on reliable energy supplies and the deteriorating situation across West Asia. Iran's effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz has disrupted India's imports of LPG and LNG — commodities on which hundreds of millions of Indian households depend. The UAE alone supplies nearly 6 per cent of India's total crude imports and ranks as the third-largest source of LPG and petroleum products.

**Why this moment matters:**
New Delhi has been running a quiet but intensive Gulf diplomacy blitz. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar recently visited the UAE, Petroleum Minister Hardeep Puri flew to Qatar, and National Security Adviser Ajit Doval made the rounds in Saudi Arabia — all to shore up supply chains before a crisis deepens. In January, India and the UAE already inked a *$3 billion LNG deal* and signed a Letter of Intent for a Strategic Defence Partnership. Modi's stopover builds directly on that momentum. The two leaders will also discuss the upcoming BRICS Summit, which India hosts in September, and the welfare of the four-million-strong Indian diaspora in the Emirates.

**What to watch next:**
After Abu Dhabi, Modi travels to Italy, Norway, Sweden and the Netherlands — watch for any formal energy or LNG supply announcements timed to coincide with, or follow, the Abu Dhabi meeting.
